answer: By modeling trust propagation as a personalized PageRank process, the spectral partition barrier of an expander graph acts as a topological reef that prevents random walks from starting to wander into adversarial regions. We bound this propagation by coupling a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function to the latency of copper hardware and staking collateral. When malicious deviations trigger slashing penalties, the resulting negative expected utility enforces a robust Nash equilibrium that secures the honest consensus.
